topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the cancer biology lecture series, the interdisciplinary student audience, and the primary learning outcomes of the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Breakdown of Cellular Differentiation and Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how accumulated genetic alterations disrupt normal developmental differentiation programs, tissue architecture, and cell-matrix boundaries.

topics.label: Characteristics of Benign, Invasive, and Metastatic Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological behavior, histological features, and clinical progression of benign lesions, tissue-invasive neoplasms, and metastatic disease.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Mechanisms of Pathogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the standard naming conventions for different neoplasm types and describe the physiological mechanisms by which tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative Cancer Incidence Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the frequency, tissue distribution, and comparative prevalence of cancer across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical Approaches and Challenges in Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, and comparative effectiveness of population screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by revisiting the stated learning outcomes and providing housekeeping instructions for upcoming sessions.
